name: THE GREENLIGHT — Solo Critic (the control)
what_this_is: The 'before' in the before/after. A SINGLE reviewer with ONE implied reader, scoring content for competence only. The council the participant builds (THE-COUNCIL.md) is measured against this. DO NOT EDIT — changing it moves both sides of the comparison.
design_driver: A single reviewer holds one implied audience — an average of everyone, a person who exists nowhere. It therefore cannot express 'good content aimed at the wrong reader' as a verdict, because it has no second reader to disagree with. The council fixes this by seating many audiences, each with its own verdict. P4 is the proof: a polished governance whitepaper filed against a store lead, which the solo critic returns as REVISE (competent) and can never see as REJECT-for-Retail / SHIP-for-Compliance at once.

values.label: Fail
values.meaning: Actively wrong or harmful to the reader.

values.label: Weak
values.meaning: Present but unreliable. A reviewer would send it back.

values.label: Adequate
values.meaning: Acceptable. Not memorable, not a problem.

values.label: Strong
values.meaning: Does the job well enough to publish as-is.

criteria.name: Accurate
criteria.question: Is every factual claim true, current, and verifiable?

anchors.0: Contains a claim that is false, or a capability that does not exist.
anchors.1: Claims stated with more confidence than the source supports, including any unverifiable capability.
anchors.2: Accurate and verifiable; a few could use a citation.
anchors.3: Every claim accurate and traceable to something real.

criteria.watch_for: Confident tone is not evidence. An unverifiable capability is a 1 or INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT, never a 2.

criteria.name: Clear
criteria.question: Can a reader follow it on one pass, without re-reading?

anchors.0: Incoherent, or steps in an unfollowable order.
anchors.1: Requires re-reading; jargon appears before it is defined.
anchors.3: Genuinely easy to follow; complexity sequenced well.

criteria.watch_for: Fluent writing that says nothing still fails this.

criteria.name: Right level
criteria.question: Is it pitched at a competent professional — not wildly too advanced or too basic?

anchors.0: Unusable for a general professional reader — far too advanced or far too basic.
anchors.2: Broadly appropriate for a competent reader.
anchors.3: Well pitched for a general professional audience.

criteria.watch_for: This criterion averages all readers into one. It CANNOT be too advanced for one audience and too basic for another at the same time — so it splits the difference and passes content that is wrong for specific readers. That blind spot is the reason the council exists.

gates: Two or more criteria at 1 or below -> REVISE (minimum).
Any criterion returned INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT -> cannot be SHIP; escalate to human.

thresholds.SHIP: Weighted average >= 2.5 and no gate triggered.
thresholds.REVISE: Weighted average >= 1.5, or any gate short of reject.
thresholds.REJECT: Weighted average < 1.5, or a fatal gate triggered.

already_scored.note: Four blind passes. One verdict per piece — the solo critic has no way to emit a per-audience verdict. This is the control the council is measured against.

pieces.tell: Competent; a claim or two wants a citation.
Reads well; can't see the segmented plant network can't reach half of it.
THE TELL. Polished governance whitepaper filed against a store lead. REJECT-for-Retail and SHIP-for-Compliance at once — one verdict cannot hold both, so it misses.
Short, followable, fine for the declared reader.

already_scored.headline: Not one solo pass flagged P4 as a reject. A single reviewer cannot say 'excellent, and wrong for this room.' A council can.

output_contract.why: The council's per-seat scorecards reuse this same shape, plus a 'seat' and a 'source' and 'confidence' per score. One contract makes the whole thing gradeable across Cowork, Studio, and VS Code.

required_fields.audience: the implied reader (solo) OR the seat (council)
